I raised this finding in round 2 (code-security-reviewer). Verified on candidate 60dd90b6 (fix ced8d9924, AN-P7F at 0326ee9ea).
(1) validate.mjs --register DG7: 'PASS register rules at DG7', exit 0 (40-validators.log). The full gate validation fails only on the missing DG7.json, as it should before the audit.
(2) The register has 412/412 rows IMPLEMENTED, and all 54 DG7-final rows are IMPLEMENTED. Each of the 18 rows has a non-empty evidence cell, cites D-274, and ends with a 'completes-after-gate:' marker naming the remaining clause. The marker texts are in 21-f935-register.log.
(3) Judgement of the Q19 extension (the user's decision D-274; the assignment asks reviewers to judge it). I accept it as an honest disclosure mechanism, and I do not treat any disclosed gap as met. Two groups:
- Remaining clause structurally after the gate: DLV-005, 014, 018, 028, 031, 039 (seal V6/V7), 040, S20-031, S21-002 and S21-004. The clause is the DG7 round, audit, gate record, seal or pipeline run itself. It cannot exist on a frozen candidate, as with the DG6 A23 precedent and D-243 Q19.
- Real, disclosed deviations: DLV-011 (C2 27 hits), DLV-012 (C3), DLV-024 (C5 1 hit), DLV-030 (A27 K11 partial) and DLV-008 (assignment hits; C4 PASS on the candidate). These are NOT literally met. They are disclosed in the register, release notes and known-limitations under the user's decisions D-249/D-270, and the release-auditor decides them at the gate.
The rows' notes say so ('Disclosed deviation, not met'; 'They are not presented as met').
One marker is inaccurate. REQ-DLV-012 says 'six' C3 hits, but the frozen candidate has seven. That stays open under F-DG7-960, see there. It is not a reason to reject the mechanism. This finding (the frozen register cannot pass validateGate) is fixed. I did not author the fix (AN-P7F).

Not closed on candidate 60dd90b6. The defect class is still there: the release's disclosure of DG7's C3 handback hits does not cover every handback in the frozen candidate.
What I ran (20-f915-f961-f960.log): node tools/release/protocol-audit.mjs --stage DG7 --root <repo> at HEAD 9c69cd11 (= source 8323dacae plus META-only freeze files). It reports C3 HIT with 7 hits (C2 27, C5 1, exit 1), and so does the orchestrator's own protocol-audit-r3.json (head 0326ee9ea). The seventh hit is docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-D8-devops-engineer.md, missing merge_instructions. Its headings are 1. Files changed … 5. Open questions; a grep for merge|rebase|integrat finds no merge-instructions text. It was committed at 6c606e5b3 (19:15Z, run exit 1, completed by DO-D8B). That is after D-270 ('every new assignment from here carries the full contract elements') and before AN-P7F wrote the register (0326ee9ea, 20:58Z).
How each disclosure stands:
- docs/handover/known-limitations.md l.62 is now right: 'C3 … DG7 | HIT | 7'.
- The shipped register row REQ-DLV-012 still says 'DG7 C3 6 hits … Disclosed deviation, not met: six DG7 implementation handbacks each lack one of the five sections. Five are the D-270 hits … The sixth, T-DG7-FE-C3…'. Its completes-after-gate marker says 'the D-270 C3 hits (six, F-DG7-960 included)'.
- release-notes.md l.35, generated from that row, repeats 'six'.
So the register and release notes understate the hits and do not name the DO-D8 handback.
Checks that stay green: check-handover (default and MTH_STRICT_HANDOVER=1) and known-limitations --check, both PASS with protocol-audit-r3.json. Neither compares the register's stated count with the report.
The FE-C3 hit that this finding first reported is now disclosed in all three places. What remains is the same mismatch for one more handback.
Severity stays Low (documentation drift in a disclosure; no product behaviour). To close it, either correct the REQ-DLV-012 notes and marker to seven and name T-DG7-DO-D8, then regenerate the release notes; or have the release-auditor and a specialist accept it as an observation. I authored no part of this.

Verified in a disposable clone of 8323dacae (DO-D8 and DO-D8B). The code (deploy/scripts/drill/cleanup.sh; transfer-drill.sh l.47-49, 99, 105-112, 134-144, 346-348, 609-612):
- The outer mode now ends with td_remove_work, which always returns 0. After five 1 s attempts it prints one WARNING line (stderr and drill.log) saying the result is unchanged, then exit $rc, so a PASS stays 0 and a FAIL stays 1.
- The EXIT trap and the D2/D9 stops use td_stop_pg on the real postmaster: SIGINT, a bounded wait for it and its /proc-listed children, then QUIT, then KILL. There is also td_stop_pg_dir via postmaster.pid, which checks comm=postgres and cwd=datadir before it signals anything.
- The rm guard refuses an empty path or '/'.
Runs (Node 24.21.0):
(1) Full harness file under with-pg.sh: 55/55, exit 0, 206 s. The real-PostgreSQL case stopped 6 processes in 0.4 s, and no postgres was left (31b-f963-harness-with-pg.log). My first run of that file (31-f963-drill-cleanup.log section A) was started without with-pg.sh by my own error: 24 DB-dependent cases failed in under 4 ms each (T-B3, T-B10, T-B16, T-B17, T-B19), 31 passed, exit 1. It is superseded by (1).
(2) The 8 T-DG7-DO-D8 cases alone: 8/8, exit 0.
(3) Revert-to-fail, mutant M1 (td_remove_work returns the rm status, the pre-fix behaviour): 3 cases fail, exit 1. The rc-0 case gets actual 1 vs expected 0, which is the reported bug.
(4) Mutant M2 (td_stop_pg sends only TERM to the launcher, the pre-fix stop_pid race): 3 cases fail, exit 1. The postmaster is still alive and postmaster.pid is still present.
(5) Sources were restored (sha256 1b2b6dfd… before and after). During M2, one mutant-started postgres was briefly counted (the line '1'); it had exited by my next check, and the later run left 0.
Not re-run by me: the full A18 drill (310 s). It needs an archive and ARCH_MB*4+1024 MB of scratch, and only 2.5 GB was free on the shared host at the time. I rely on DO-D8B's t-b11-run.log and the QA A18 driver for that. The harness tests and mutants above prove the fix's mechanism. I did not author this fix.
